summary: Check whether a string reads the same forwards and backwards after lowercasing and ignoring non-alphanumeric characters.
mainInsight: A palindrome mirrors around its centre, so compare from both ends moving inward, skipping characters that do not count; there is no need to build a cleaned copy.

approaches.name: Clean then reverse
approaches.summary: Filter to alphanumerics, lowercase, compare with its reverse.

approaches.name: Two pointers in place
approaches.summary: l and r move inward, skipping non-alphanumerics, comparing lowercase characters.

personalSolution.notes: Pointer logic is right. Lowercase per character to get true O(1) extra space.

promptVariants: Which technique checks a palindrome in O(1) extra space?
cards.explanation: Position i must match position n-1-i; two converging pointers do exactly that.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Hash map of counts: Counts ignore order (that tests rearrangeability, not palindromes).

promptVariants: What is true about s[0..l-1] and s[r+1..n-1] at every step?
What has already been verified outside the [l, r] range at each iteration?
cards.answer: Every alphanumeric character in the already-processed prefix and suffix has been matched against its mirror, so everything outside [l, r] is verified.
cards.explanation: Termination when l crosses r means every pair matched.

promptVariants: Time complexity of the two-pointer solution: ___
Valid Palindrome with two pointers runs in ___ time.
cards.explanation: Each pointer moves at most n steps in total.

promptVariants: Your solution calls s.lower(). What does that do to space, and how could you avoid it?
How could you make your Valid Palindrome solution truly O(1) extra space?
cards.answer: s.lower() builds a new string, so extra space is O(n). To get O(1), keep s and call .lower() on the individual characters during comparison (or compare c.lower()).

promptVariants: Why does the loop skip with `elif`s in this order, and why `while l <= r` vs `l < r`?
How does the two-pointer loop handle punctuation, and what happens when l == r?
cards.answer: Non-alphanumerics are skipped one pointer at a time until both point at real characters, then compared. `l <= r` is harmless (a single middle character always matches itself); `l < r` is equivalent and slightly tighter.
keyPoints: Skip one side until both valid
l == r is a trivially valid middle
cards.explanation: The order of branches does not change correctness.

promptVariants: What should the function return for the string " " or ".,"?
How should a string with no alphanumerics be treated?
options: True - the cleaned string is empty
cards.answer: True - the cleaned string is empty
cards.explanation: An empty cleaned string reads the same forwards and backwards.

incorrectOptionExplanations.False - nothing to compare: The empty string is a palindrome by definition.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It raises an error: The pointers just cross without indexing errors.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Depends on the length: No - all punctuation-only inputs are palindromes.
